## The critical path

Quoted verbatim from `CLAUDE.md`, which owns the ordering.

**This section owns the ordering and says nothing about progress** — landed status is derived onto
`state-of-play.md` from the architecture docs' ✅ headings, and a second copy here would go stale between
merges. Route order; numbers are stable labels; `roadmap-v2.md` §3a is the same route with the *why*.

5b. "Can't" effects (CR 101.2/614.17/613.11) and 5c. copy effects (CR 707/712/708/729 + Layer 1): the phases their docs name, at their steps below
6. Triggered abilities (CR 603): the rest of `roadmap-v2.md` §3a's A rows
**After 6, in order** (`roadmap-v2.md` §3a, "From triggers to v0.5", has each step's why):
`route-review`; the item 6 audit's readiness; `card-layer-cleanup`; `pausing-at-a-decision`'s design; `modes-plus-choice-kinds`; `linked-abilities`; `resolution-recipients-and-amounts`; `information-model-design`, `information-model`;
`permission-design` with `card-and-object-model` beside it; `command-zone-casting`; `game-formats`; `multiplayer-rules`; `cant-be-targeted`; `cant-cast-play-or-activate`;
`combat-restrictions`, `cant-pay-costs`, `combat-requirements`; `as-though-effects`'s permission half; `layers-combat-and-counters`; `rulings-for-every-card`;
then `tarkir-dragonstorm-decks`: its gap census; `mana-ability-costs`, `any-color-plus-painlands-plus-signets`, `chosen-color-plus-could-produce`, `convoke-delve-improvise`, `hybrid-and-phyrexian-payment`, `remaining-costs`;
`casting-from-other-zones`; `token-copies`, `spell-copies`; the card model's split, face-down and player-Aura builds; the five decks; `mana-payment-solver`.
**v0.5 is Tarkir: Dragonstorm Commander's five decks at one five-seat table**, in the dev GUI and over the CLI (owner, 2026-10-29).
After it, ordered at its close: the rest of the route's rows, wider card work and Phase 9's remainder; then Phase 10.
**v1 is two use cases** (owner, 2026-08-24): 4-player Commander through the GUI built for players, Phase 10, which is when
v1 is done (2026-10-29), and highly parallel AI games over the CLI. **Write new systems N-player-shaped from the start**.

## Debt — `codebase-state.md`'s Deferred Migrations

| | |
|---|---:|
| Numbered items | 402 |
| …closed, still recorded | 248 |
| …open — unreachable, and says why | 106 |
| **…open — reachable, wrong today** | **4** |
| …open — reachable, not wrong (perf, a name, a harness) | 30 |
| …open — nothing to build, a record for a later phase | 14 |
| **…open — reachability *not* stated** | **0** |
| …open, carrying an explicit `**Sized:**` | 152 of 154 |

Two bolded rows. "Not stated" is the one to act on: an item that does not say
why it cannot bite yet is an unchecked claim rather than a deferral. "Wrong
today" is the list of known wrong answers a fuzz game can reach — bug
reports filed as deferrals, each named in the section. A dated
`**Reachability (YYYY-MM-DD):**` line is what the board reads; the date says
when the verdict was last derived against the tree, because reachability
only ever grows.

Where each open item is homed, read off its `**Slotted:**` line:

| | |
|---|---:|
| …slotted to a phase or roadmap row still to come | 142 |
| …a record, nothing to build | 12 |
| **…open with no home** | **0** |
| **A number used twice in one run** | **0** |

**Both bolded rows fail the check.** A home is a `**Slotted:**` line naming a
phase or `roadmap-v2.md` §3a row still to come (Phases 9 and 10 by number,
having no rows yet), or "none — a record". "With the first registered card
that …" is no home since #294's review. A line naming only phases that have landed is
no home: they went without it. A phase reads its intake list at its first
ticket: `python plans/check_state_of_play.py --slotted cant-be-targeted`.

### This is not `specdb owed`, and the two overlap nowhere

| | `specdb owed` | Deferred Migrations |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | an **atom** — one scenario from the spec corpus | a **migration** — one code change |
| Looks | **backwards**, at phases already shipped | **forwards**, at systems not yet built |
| Catches | a phase that closed without testing its own spec | scaffolding that will lie to whatever is built on it |
| Reachable now | yes, by construction — the behaviour shipped | usually not, which is why it is easy to forget |
| Gate | a phase does not close until it is clean | read before a system's first ticket |

**The seam between them is real.** A defect in shipped behaviour that has no
atom is in neither list — RC-5's item 61 is one, because the ruling it violates
was never written into the corpus. And `owed`'s default scope is `SHIPPED_PHASES`,
which gained Phase 6 only at the post-RE audit (2026-09-15): until then a
replacement phase closing against "owed is clean" was making a claim about three
*other* phases, and what actually gated it was the `// COVERS:` annotation
discipline. → `engineering-practices.md#the-spec-database`.
